mainTopic: Pregnancy foods, a wife's duty to nurse, the maidservant exemptions, the three personal tasks and נדה, and sharing food with the waiter
overview: This amud opens by finishing a list of foods a pregnant woman eats and the good traits they give her children, with a story about the fragrant daughter of שבור מלכא. Then רב הונא reports a question about nursing: when husband and wife disagree, whose family custom decides? The answer is the rule that a wife 'goes up with her husband but does not go down with him,' backed by two פסוקים. Next the גמרא returns to the משנה about maidservants a wife brings into the marriage. It explains step by step why one, two, or three maidservants free her from only some housework, and why four free her from all of it. Even then, רב הונא says she still pours his cup, makes his bed, and washes his face, hands, and feet. A wife who is a נדה skips exactly these three personal tasks, with some limits and changes. The amud ends with rules and stories about sharing food with the waiter at a meal, so that he does not suffer from craving. A story at the king's gate begins and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Foods during pregnancy and the children's traits
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes a list of foods a pregnant woman eats and the good trait each one gives her children.
steps.simpleTranslation: ...healthy children. One who eats eggs has children with large eyes. One who eats fish has graceful children. One who eats celery has beautiful children. One who eats coriander has well-fleshed children. One who eats אתרוג has sweet-smelling children.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a list it started on the previous amud: what a pregnant woman eats affects how her children turn out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each food is paired with one trait in the child. The first word, 'healthy,' is the end of a line from the previous amud. This is guidance and practical wisdom, not a legal ruling.

phrases.english: ...healthy children.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָכְלָה בֵּיעֵי — הָווּ לַהּ בְּנֵי עֵינָנֵי.
phrases.english: One who eats eggs will have large-eyed children.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָכְלָה כְּווֹרֵי — הָווּ לַהּ בְּנֵי חִינָּנֵי.
phrases.english: One who eats fish will have graceful children.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָכְלָה כַּרְפְּסָא — הָווּ לַהּ בְּנֵי זִיוְתָנֵי.
phrases.english: One who eats celery will have beautiful children.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָכְלָה כּוּסְבַּרְתָּא — הָווּ לַהּ בְּנֵי בִּישְׂרָנֵי.
phrases.english: One who eats coriander will have well-fleshed children.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָכְלָה אֶתְרוֹגָא — הָווּ לַהּ בְּנֵי רֵיחָנֵי.
phrases.english: One who eats אתרוג will have sweet-smelling children.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָכְלָה בֵּיעֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a list begun before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Specific foods eaten during pregnancy give the children specific good traits.

steps.title: The fragrant daughter of King Shapur
steps.stepSummary: A story shows the אתרוג claim in action: the daughter of שבור מלכא smelled so good that she was placed among the spices.
steps.simpleTranslation: The daughter of שבור מלכא: her mother ate אתרוג while pregnant with her, and they used to bring her before her father at the top of all the spices.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short story that illustrates the last item on the list, eating אתרוג.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story backs up the claim that eating אתרוג leads to sweet-smelling children. The girl's scent was so strong that she was treated like the finest of the spices.

phrases.english: The daughter of King Shapur:
her mother ate אתרוג while pregnant with her,
and they would bring her before her father
at the top of the spices.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּרַתֵּיה דְּשַׁבּוּר מַלְכָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Illustrates the final item (אתרוג) in Step 1.
steps.raayaObject: Eating אתרוג during pregnancy produces sweet-smelling children.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of the daughter of שבור מלכא.

steps.title: She wants to nurse and he does not
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא reports a test from רב הונא בר חיננא: if the wife wants to nurse and the husband does not, we follow her, because she is the one in pain.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: רב הונא בר חיננא tested us. If she says she will nurse and he says she should not, we listen to her, because it is her pain.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. רב הונא reports the first, easy case of a question he was tested on: a disagreement about nursing where the wife wants to nurse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If she wants to nurse and is stopped, she is the one who suffers physically. So her wish wins. This simple case sets up the harder case in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: he tested us (posed a question to check our understanding)
we listen to her (her wish decides)

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:

phrases.aramaic: בְּדַק לַן רַב הוּנָא בַּר חִינָּנָא:
phrases.english: Rav Huna bar Chinana tested us:
If she says she will nurse,
and he says she should not nurse,
we listen to her.
It is her pain.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא, בְּדַק לַן רַב הוּנָא בַּר חִינָּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new halachic topic after the aggadic list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the wife wants to nurse and the husband objects, her wish is followed because she would suffer.

steps.title: He wants her to nurse and she refuses
steps.stepSummary: The harder case: the husband wants her to nurse and she does not want to. What is the law?
steps.simpleTranslation: If he says she should nurse and she says she will not nurse, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: Now the question flips the case around: the husband wants nursing and the wife refuses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the 'her pain' reason from Step 3 does not apply, since refusing to nurse causes her no suffering. So it is unclear whether she has to do what he wants.

phrases.english: If he says she should nurse,
and she says she will not nurse, what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: הוּא אוֹמֵר לְהָנִיק, וְהִיא אוֹמֶרֶת שֶׁלֹּא לְהָנִיק, מַהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reverses the case of Step 3.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Must a wife nurse when her husband wants her to and she refuses?

steps.title: If it is not her family's custom, we follow her
steps.stepSummary: Part of the question is answered: wherever nursing is not her family's way, we listen to her.
steps.simpleTranslation: Anywhere that it is not her way, we listen to her.
steps.whatsHappening: The question is narrowed. One part is easy: if the women of her family don't usually nurse, she doesn't have to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This settles the case where nursing is not her custom. What remains is the case where her family does nurse but his family does not. That is the real question, asked in the next step and answered in Step 7.

keyTerms.meaning: anywhere that, in any case where

phrases.english: Anywhere that it is not her way,
phrases.notes: 'Her way' means the women of her family don't normally nurse their own babies.

phrases.english: we listen to her.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֹּל הֵיכָא דְּלָאו אוֹרְחַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the easy part of Step 4's question and narrows what remains.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: If nursing is not her family's custom, she need not nurse.

steps.title: Her family nurses, his does not: whom do we follow?
steps.stepSummary: The real question: if nursing is her family's custom but not his, do we follow his custom or hers?
steps.simpleTranslation: If it is her way but not his way, what is the law? Do we follow his custom or hers?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states the sharp version of the question: the two families have different customs, so which family decides?
steps.deeperAnalysis: By her own family's standard she should nurse, but by his family's standard she wouldn't. The question is whose standard counts once she is married to him.

keyTerms.meaning: we go after his (we follow his custom)

phrases.aramaic: הִיא אוֹרְחַהּ וְהוּא לָאו אוֹרְחֵיהּ, מַאי?
phrases.english: If it is her way and not his way, what is the law?
Do we follow his custom,
or do we follow hers?

steps.triggerLanguage: הִיא אוֹרְחַהּ וְהוּא לָאו אוֹרְחֵיהּ, מַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sharpens the question that remains after Step 5. Step 7 answers it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: When the wife's family nurses but the husband's does not, which family's custom decides?

steps.title: She goes up with him but not down with him
steps.stepSummary: The question is solved from the rule that a wife rises to her husband's higher status but does not drop to a lower one, so she follows his custom and need not nurse.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we solved it for him from this: she goes up with him and does not go down with him.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא reports how they answered the test: with the well-known rule that a wife goes up with her husband but does not go down with him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Not nursing counts as the more comfortable, higher standard. Since his family's women don't nurse, she rises to his level and is exempt. The rule only ever helps her: she gains from his higher standard and never loses from a lower one.

keyTerms.meaning: she goes up with him (to his higher standard)
she does not go down with him

steps.whatToRemember: A wife 'עולה עמו ואינה יורדת עמו': she gets the benefit of her husband's higher standard but never loses her own. So if his family doesn't nurse, she doesn't have to either.

phrases.english: And we solved it for him from this:
She goes up with him and does not go down with him.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּפָשֵׁיטְנָא לֵיהּ מֵהָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: She follows his higher standard, so she need not nurse.
steps.whyThisMatters: The rule of עולה עמו ואינה יורדת עמו is a basic principle in the laws of a wife's support and status.

steps.title: רב הונא's source: 'בעולת בעל'
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא brings a פסוק for the rule: 'בעולת בעל' is read as hinting at the husband's rising (עלייה), not his descent.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: What is the verse? 'And she is a man's wife (בעולת בעל)': with the rising of the husband, and not with the descent of the husband.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא gives a פסוק as the source for the rule 'she goes up with him but not down with him.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word בעולת sounds like עלייה, rising. So the פסוק is read as saying that she shares in her husband's rising, and by implication not in his falling.

keyTerms.meaning: what is the verse (that teaches this)?

phrases.english: Rav Huna said: What is the verse?
"And she is a man's wife."
With the rising of the husband,
phrases.notes: A play on words: בעולת sounds like עלייה, 'rising.'

phrases.english: and not with the descent of the husband.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: מַאי קְרָאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides a scriptural source for the rule in Step 7.
steps.raayaObject: A wife goes up with her husband but not down with him.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר's source: 'mother of all living'
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר brings a different פסוק: חוה was 'the mother of all living,' meaning a wife was given for life, not for suffering.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said it comes from here: 'For she was the mother of all living.' She was given for life, and not given for pain.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר offers a second, different פסוק as a source for the same rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reads 'mother of all חי' as teaching that a wife was given to her husband for a good life, not for hardship. So she shares his good fortune but does not have to sink with him into a harder life.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said it comes from here:
"For she was the mother of all living."
She was given for life,
and not given for pain.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר מֵהָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers an alternative source to רב הונא's in Step 8.
steps.raayaObject: A wife goes up with her husband but not down with him.
steps.raayaSupportSource: בראשית 3:20, 'כי היא היתה אם כל חי'.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Two פסוקים are given for the same rule; both agree a wife shares her husband's rise but not his fall.

steps.title: The משנה about one maidservant: she still does the other tasks
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about a wife who brought one maidservant and infers that she still has to do the remaining tasks.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'If she brought him one maidservant,' and so on. This implies she does the other tasks.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה and draws an inference from it. This sets up the challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה exempts her from only some jobs (grinding, baking, laundering). So the גמרא reads it as saying that she still must do the rest of the housework herself.

keyTerms.meaning: she brought into the marriage for him

phrases.english: "If she brought him one maidservant," and so on.
This implies she does the other tasks.

steps.triggerLanguage: הִכְנִיסָה לוֹ שִׁפְחָה וְכוּ׳
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the משנה after the nursing discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A wife who brought one maidservant is exempt from some tasks but still does the others.

steps.title: Shouldn't the maidservant count as her replacement?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: let her tell him, 'I brought you a woman in my place,' and be exempt from everything.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let her say to him: I brought you a woman in my place!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the inference: the maidservant should replace the wife fully, so why does the wife do any work?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The argument is that she provided a full worker to stand in for her. If so, the maidservant should cover all of the wife's duties, not just some.

keyTerms.meaning: but let her say to him
in my place, as my replacement

phrases.english: But let her say to him:
I brought you a woman in my place!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתֵימָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the inference of Step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: The inference that a wife with one maidservant still does the remaining tasks.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The maidservant is a full substitute for the wife, so the wife should be fully exempt.

steps.title: The maidservant works to cover herself, so who covers the wife?
steps.stepSummary: The husband can answer that the maidservant's work only covers what he spends on her; someone still has to work to cover the wife's own support.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because he can say to her: This one works for me and for herself. For you, who works?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: the maidservant is not a full replacement, because her work pays for her own keep.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The husband now has to feed and support the maidservant too, so her work only balances out what she costs. The wife's own support still needs to be earned, so she must still do some tasks.
steps.whatToRemember: A maidservant the wife brings covers only her own keep plus some tasks. The wife still does some work, which goes toward her own support.

phrases.english: Because he can say to her:
This one works for me and for herself,
but for you, who works?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם דְּאָמַר לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejects the premise that the maidservant is a full substitute.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The maidservant fully replaces the wife, so the wife does no work.
steps.terutzMaskana: The maidservant's work offsets her own support; the wife must still work for hers.

steps.title: Two maidservants: no cooking or nursing, but other tasks remain
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's case of two maidservants and infers that the wife still does the other tasks.
steps.simpleTranslation: If she brought two maidservants, she does not cook and does not nurse. This implies she still does the rest of the tasks.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה, about two maidservants, and points out what it implies. This sets up the next question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two maidservants free the wife from cooking and nursing. But the wording suggests she must still do the remaining tasks, like making the bed and working wool. This is the same pattern the גמרא used for one maidservant in Step 10.

phrases.english: If she brought two, she does not cook
and does not nurse, etc.
This implies she does do the rest.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא שְׁאָרָא עָבְדָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the one-maidservant case (Steps 10-12) to the two-maidservant case in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With two maidservants, the wife is free from cooking and nursing but still does the remaining tasks.

steps.title: Why can't she say the two maidservants cover everything?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: one maidservant can work for the wife and herself, and the other for the husband and herself, so the wife should do nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let her tell him: I brought you one woman who works for me and for herself, and another who works for you and for herself!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the inference from Step 13. If each maidservant covers two people, the wife should be free from all work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 12 said a maidservant's work only pays for her own upkeep, with someone still needed to cover the wife's support. Now the wife argues that two maidservants solve this. One covers the wife plus herself, and the other covers the husband plus herself, so nothing is left for the wife.

phrases.english: But let her say to him: I brought you
another woman who toils
for me and for herself,
and one for you and for herself!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתֵימָא לֵיהּ: עַיֵּילִית לָךְ אִיתְּתָא אַחֲרִיתִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the inference of Step 13 using the logic of Step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The inference that a wife with two maidservants still does the remaining tasks.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two maidservants can cover the support of both the wife and the husband, so she should not have to work at all.

steps.title: Someone still has to serve the guests
steps.stepSummary: The husband can answer: who will do the work for the guests and travelers who visit?
steps.simpleTranslation: Because he can say to her: who will toil for the guests and passing travelers?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that a household with servants also gets guests. Those guests create extra work that the two maidservants do not cover.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wife's math only counted the husband, the wife, and the maidservants. A larger household also attracts visitors. That extra work is why she still has some tasks left.

phrases.english: Because he can say to her:
Who will toil for the guests and passing travelers?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם דְּאָמַר לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Adds a factor the challenge left out: guests create extra work.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Two maidservants cover everyone in the house, so the wife does nothing.
steps.terutzMaskana: Guests and travelers add work, so the wife still does the remaining tasks.

steps.title: Three maidservants: no bed-making, but other tasks remain
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's case of three maidservants and infers that the wife still does the other tasks.
steps.simpleTranslation: If she brought three, she does not make the bed. This implies she still does the rest.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the three-maidservant line of the משנה and makes the same kind of inference. This sets up another question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With three maidservants, the wife no longer has to make the bed or work wool. The wording again suggests some tasks are still left for her.

phrases.english: If she brought three, she does not make the bed.
This implies she does do the rest.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא שְׁאָרָא עָבְדָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the two-maidservant case to the three-maidservant case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With three maidservants, the wife is free from making the bed but still does the remaining tasks.

steps.title: Why doesn't the third maidservant handle the guests?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: the third maidservant can take care of the guests, so the wife should do nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let her tell him: I brought you another one for the guests and travelers!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges Step 16 using the answer from Step 15. If guests were the problem, the third maidservant solves it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 15 said guests create the leftover work. Now there is a third maidservant just for them. So the wife argues that nothing is left for her to do.

phrases.english: But let her say to him: I brought you another one
for the guests and travelers!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתֵימָא לֵיהּ: עַיֵּילִית לָךְ אַחֲרִיתִי לְאוֹרְחֵי וּפָרְחֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the answer of Step 15 to challenge the inference of Step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: The inference that a wife with three maidservants still does the remaining tasks.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The third maidservant covers the guests, which was the only leftover work, so the wife should be fully free.

steps.title: A bigger household brings more guests
steps.stepSummary: The husband answers: the more people in the house, the more guests come.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because he can say to her: the more members of the household, the more guests and travelers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that adding maidservants grows the household. A bigger household draws even more guests, so there is still work left.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra work does not stay fixed. As the house gets bigger, the guest load grows too. One maidservant for guests is still not enough.

phrases.english: Because he can say to her:
When the household members increase,
the guests and travelers increase.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם דְּאָמַר לַהּ: נְפִישׁ בְּנֵי בֵיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the leftover work grows along with the household.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One maidservant for guests covers all the extra work.
steps.terutzMaskana: A bigger house brings more guests, so the wife still has some tasks.

steps.title: Then even with four she should have to work
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: by this logic, even four maidservants would never be enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, then even with four as well!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the last answer against the משנה. If more maidservants always bring more guests, the wife should still work even with four.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says that with four maidservants the wife sits free of all tasks. But Step 18's logic seems to have no end: each new maidservant grows the house and brings more guests. So why does four free her completely?

phrases.english: If so, then even with four as well!
phrases.notes: He means: she should still have to work even with four. But the משנה says four free her completely.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, אֲפִילּוּ אַרְבַּע נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reasoning of Step 18 by pushing it to the four-maidservant case.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reasoning that more household members always means more work for the wife.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If that logic is true, four maidservants would also not free her. That goes against the משנה.

steps.title: Four maidservants help each other
steps.stepSummary: With four, there are enough of them to help one another and finish all the work.
steps.simpleTranslation: With four, since there are many of them, they help one another.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that four is a turning point. With that many workers, they can share the load and cover everything.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With three, each maidservant has her own job, and the extra guests still leave a gap. With four, the group is big enough to pitch in for each other. That covers the growing work, so the wife is fully free.
steps.whatToRemember: One, two, or three maidservants each free the wife from more tasks. Only four free her from everything, because four are enough to help each other with all the work.

phrases.english: With four, since there are many of them,
they help one another.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַרְבַּע, כֵּיוָן דִּנְפִישִׁי לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 19 and wraps up the analysis of the maidservant counts.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points to a group effect: at four, the workers can cover for each other.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every added maidservant just adds more work, so the wife can never be fully free.
steps.terutzMaskana: Four maidservants can help each other with all the work, so the wife is free of all tasks.

steps.title: It is enough that she could afford to bring maidservants
steps.stepSummary: רב חנא (or רבי שמואל בר נחמני) says the משנה does not require actually bringing maidservants. It is enough that her dowry could pay for them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חנא, and some say רבי שמואל בר נחמני, said: it does not mean she actually brought them. Rather, once she is able to bring them, she is exempt even if she did not bring them.
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement explains the משנה's words 'she brought him.' It is enough that she had the means to bring maidservants.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now, the case sounded like real maidservants walking into the house. רב חנא says what matters is the dowry's value. If it was big enough to buy maidservants, she gets the same exemption even without them.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not read 'she brought him maidservants' only as real servants arriving. Here it means she had enough in her dowry to pay for them.
steps.whyThisMatters: This makes the exemption depend on how much money she brought, not on servants physically being there.

phrases.english: רב חנא said,
and some say it was רבי שמואל בר נחמני:
It does not mean she actually brought them to him,
rather, once she is able to bring them,
even though she did not bring them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חָנָא וְאִיתֵּימָא רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the counting of maidservants and explains what 'brought' means in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A wife whose dowry could pay for maidservants gets the exemption, even if she did not actually bring them.

steps.title: A ברייתא: bringing them or saving up for them is the same
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that it makes no difference whether she brought maidservants or cut back on her own spending to provide one.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: whether she brought them to him, or whether she cut back from her own to provide for him, it is the same.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that backs up and widens רב חנא's point. Saving money to provide a maidservant counts just like bringing one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חנא said real servants are not needed. The ברייתא adds another case: a wife who freed up money by spending less on herself. She also gets the exemption, which shows that what counts is the value she provides.
steps.whatToRemember: The wife's exemption comes from the value she brings to the house. Real maidservants, a dowry large enough to buy them, or money saved from her own needs all count.

phrases.english: It was taught: whether she brought them to him,
or whether she cut back from her own for him.
phrases.notes: Literally 'squeezed': she spent less on herself to free up money for a maidservant.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא: אֶחָד שֶׁהִכְנִיסָה לוֹ, וְאֶחָד שֶׁצִּמְצְמָה לוֹ מִשֶּׁלָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא that supports and widens the statement of Step 21.
steps.raayaObject: רב חנא's point that the wife does not need to physically bring maidservants.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that treats a wife who saved from her own needs the same as one who brought maidservants.

steps.title: Even a wife who sits in a chair still does three personal tasks
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא teaches that even a wife with four maidservants must still pour her husband's cup, make his bed, and wash his face, hands, and feet.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says that with four maidservants she may sit in a chair. רב יצחק בר חנניא said in the name of רב הונא: even though they said she may sit in a chair, she still pours his cup, makes his bed, and washes his face, hands, and feet.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה's line about four maidservants. רב הונא adds that three personal tasks still stay her job.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה freed her from housework once there are enough maidservants. רב הונא explains that these three tasks are not ordinary housework. They are personal acts of closeness between wife and husband, so a maidservant cannot take them over.

keyTerms.meaning: A chair. Here it means a wife who does not have to do housework.
Pours a cup (of wine) for him

steps.whyThisMatters: These same three tasks come back right away in the rules of נדה.

phrases.english: Four: she sits in a chair.
phrases.notes: This is quoted from the משנה: a wife who brought four maidservants does not have to do housework.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יִצְחָק בַּר חֲנַנְיָא אָמַר רַב הוּנָא:
phrases.english: Rav Yitzchak bar Chananya said that Rav Huna said:

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאָמְרוּ יוֹשֶׁבֶת בְּקָתֶדְרָא,
phrases.english: Even though they said she sits in a chair,
she still pours him a cup,
and makes the bed for him,
and washes his face, his hands, and his feet for him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אף על פי שאמרו יושבת בקתדרא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the משנה's four-maidservant case and sets a limit on what 'sitting in a chair' means.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even when she is free from housework, she must still pour his cup, make his bed, and wash his face, hands, and feet.

steps.title: A נדה may do every task for her husband except the three personal ones
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא teaches that a wife who is a נדה may do all tasks for her husband except pouring his cup, making his bed, and washing his face, hands, and feet.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יצחק בר חנניא said in the name of רב הונא: every task a wife does for her husband, a נדה may also do for him, except pouring the cup, making the bed, and washing his face, hands, and feet.
steps.whatsHappening: A second teaching from the same רב הונא, about the same three tasks. This time it is about a wife who is a נדה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These three tasks are acts of closeness. During נדה, when the couple must keep apart, such closeness could lead to forbidden intimacy, so she should not do them. Ordinary work around the house is still fine.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman in her monthly period of separation from her husband

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean a נדה stops serving her husband in general. She keeps doing all normal tasks. Only these three personal ones are left out.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יִצְחָק בַּר חֲנַנְיָא אָמַר רַב הוּנָא:
phrases.english: Rav Yitzchak bar Chananya said that Rav Huna said:
All tasks that a wife does for her husband,
a niddah may do for her husband,
except for pouring the cup,
and making the bed,
and washing his face, hands, and feet.

steps.triggerLanguage: כל מלאכות שהאשה עושה לבעלה נדה עושה לבעלה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same three personal tasks from step 23 and applies them to the laws of נדה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A נדה may do every task for her husband except pouring his cup, making his bed, and washing his face, hands, and feet.

steps.title: Making the bed is only a problem when he is there
steps.stepSummary: רבא limits the bed-making rule: a נדה may not make his bed in front of him, but when he is not there it is no problem.
steps.simpleTranslation: About making the bed, רבא said: we only said this when it is in front of him. When it is not in front of him, we have no problem with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא zooms in on one of the three tasks, making the bed. רבא narrows when it is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry is about closeness between them. If he is not there to see her making his bed, that closeness is missing, so the rule does not apply.

keyTerms.meaning: In front of him, while he is there
We have no problem with it

phrases.english: And making the bed:
phrases.notes: The גמרא is picking up this one item from the list in step 24.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבָא: לָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא בְּפָנָיו,
phrases.english: Rava said: We only said this when it is in front of him,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל שֶׁלֹּא בְּפָנָיו — לֵית לַן בַּהּ.
phrases.english: but when it is not in front of him, we have no problem with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: לא אמרן אלא בפניו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows one item from רב הונא's נדה list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ban on a נדה making her husband's bed applies only when he is present.

steps.title: How the wives of the אמוראים changed the way they gave the cup
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tells how the wives of שמואל, אביי, רבא, and רב פפא served the cup in a different way during נדה.
steps.simpleTranslation: About pouring the cup: שמואל's wife would change it for him by using her left hand. אביי's wife would put it on the mouth of a barrel. רבא's wife put it on his pillow. רב פפא's wife put it on the bench.
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא looks at the cup rule. It shows real examples of how these wives still served the cup, but in a changed way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These stories show that the cup ban is about the normal, affectionate way of serving it. When she does it differently, the change reminds them both of her status. That takes away the worry, so they did it this way.

keyTerms.meaning: Changes, does it in a different way

steps.whatToRemember: The three personal tasks stay with every wife, even one with many maidservants. During נדה she skips them. Making the bed is only a problem in front of him, and the cup may be given in a changed way.

phrases.english: And pouring the cup:

phrases.aramaic: שְׁמוּאֵל מְחַלְּפָא לֵיהּ דְּבֵיתְהוּ בִּידָא דִשְׂמָאלָא.
phrases.english: Shmuel: his wife would change it for him by using her left hand.
Abaye: his wife would place it for him on the mouth of a barrel.
Rava: on the pillow.
phrases.notes: The גמרא leaves out the words but means the same as before: his wife would put the cup there.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa: on the bench.

steps.triggerLanguage: שמואל מחלפא ליה דביתהו בידא דשמאלא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the bed rule to the cup rule and shows how people actually practiced it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A נדה may give her husband his cup if she changes the normal way of doing it.

steps.title: A waiter may be made to wait for everything except meat and wine
steps.stepSummary: Another teaching of רב הונא: you may delay giving the waiter any food until later, except meat and wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יצחק בר חנניא said in the name of רב הונא: everything may be held back in front of the waiter, except meat and wine.
steps.whatsHappening: Because it was quoting teachings of רב יצחק בר חנניא, the גמרא now brings one more of his teachings on a new topic: the waiter at a meal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A waiter serving food usually eats later, after the guests. Meat and wine are different. Seeing and smelling them makes a person crave them strongly, so it would be painful to make the waiter wait. He should get some right away.

keyTerms.meaning: Waiter, the one serving the meal

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יִצְחָק בַּר חֲנַנְיָא אָמַר רַב הוּנָא:
phrases.english: Rav Yitzchak bar Chananya said that Rav Huna said:
All foods may be held back in front of the waiter,
phrases.notes: He means the waiter may be made to wait and eat these foods later.

phrases.english: except for meat and wine.

steps.triggerLanguage: הכל משהין בפני השמש חוץ מבשר ויין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic, connected only because it is another teaching from the same speakers.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A waiter may be made to wait for every food except meat and wine.

steps.title: Only fatty meat and aged wine
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא explains that the exception means only fatty meat and aged wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: this means fatty meat and aged wine.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא narrows רב הונא's exception from step 27.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Not all meat and wine stir up strong craving. Fatty meat and aged wine have a strong smell and taste. Only those make waiting truly painful for the waiter.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: בָּשָׂר שָׁמֵן וְיַיִן יָשָׁן.
phrases.english: Rav Chisda said: Fatty meat and aged wine.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רב חסדא בשר שמן ויין ישן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines which meat and wine רב הונא meant.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The waiter's exception applies only to fatty meat and aged wine.

steps.title: Fatty meat all year, aged wine only in summer
steps.stepSummary: רבא adds that fatty meat is an exception all year long, but aged wine only during the season of תמוז.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: fatty meat, all year round. Aged wine, only in the season of תמוז.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא adds a time limit to רב חסדא's definition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Fatty meat always stirs up craving, so it is never held back from the waiter. Aged wine is held back except in the hot summer season of תמוז. Then its smell spreads more strongly, so making the waiter wait would be painful.

keyTerms.meaning: The season of תמוז, the summer

steps.whatToRemember: A waiter may be made to wait for most foods. Fatty meat must not be held back from him at any time of year. Aged wine must not be held back from him in the summer.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבָא: בָּשָׂר שָׁמֵן — כׇּל הַשָּׁנָה כּוּלָּהּ,
phrases.english: Rava said: Fatty meat, the entire year,
aged wine, in the season of Tammuz.

steps.triggerLanguage: בשר שמן כל השנה כולה יין ישן בתקופת תמוז
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a time limit to רב חסדא's definition.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Fatty meat is never held back from the waiter. Aged wine is not held back from him in the summer season of תמוז.

steps.title: רב ענן's story: the mushroom dish
steps.stepSummary: רב ענן בר תחליפא tells that he was once standing before שמואל when a mushroom dish was brought. If שמואל had not given him some, he would have been in danger.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ענן בר תחליפא said: I was once standing before מר שמואל, and they brought him a cooked dish of mushrooms. If he had not given me some, I would have been in danger.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a personal story to show that other foods besides meat and wine can cause dangerous craving.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא and רבא limited the exception to fatty meat and aged wine. This story widens the list: a mushroom dish can also stir a craving strong enough to be dangerous. So the person serving must not be made to wait for it.

keyTerms.meaning: I would have been in danger
I was standing before him (serving him)

phrases.english: Rav Anan bar Tachlifa said:
I was standing before Mar Shmuel,
and they brought him a cooked dish of mushrooms,
and if he had not given me some, I would have been in danger.
phrases.notes: The danger comes from the strong craving he felt while watching the food served.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב עָנָן בַּר תַּחְלִיפָא: הֲוָה קָאֵימְנָא קַמֵּיהּ דְּמָר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another food to the list of exceptions that must be given to the waiter right away.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A mushroom dish also causes dangerous craving, so it must be shared with the one serving.

steps.title: רב אשי's story: turnip in vinegar
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי tells that he stood before רב כהנא when turnip slices in vinegar were brought. Without a taste, he would have been in danger.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: I was once standing before רב כהנא, and they brought him slices of turnip in vinegar. If he had not given me some, I would have been in danger.
steps.whatsHappening: A second, matching story adds another food that causes dangerous craving.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story has the same pattern as רב ענן's. This time the food is sharp and sour, turnip in vinegar, not something with a smell. This prepares for the general rule that will mention both smell and sharpness.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
I was standing before Rav Kahana,
and they brought him slices of turnip in vinegar,
and if he had not given me some, I would have been in danger.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: הֲוָה קָאֵימְנָא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב כָּהֲנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel story adding a sharp, sour food to the list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Turnip in vinegar also causes dangerous craving and must be shared.

steps.title: רב פפא: even a fragrant date
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says that even a fragrant date must be offered to the one serving.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Even a fragrant date.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא pushes the list further and includes even something as small as a sweet-smelling date.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word "even" shows this is the smallest case. A date is a simple, cheap food, but if its smell is strong it can still cause craving. So you might think only big dishes count, and רב פפא teaches that size does not matter.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
Even a fragrant date.
phrases.notes: He means: even this must be given right away to the person serving.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב פָּפָּא אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ תְּמַרְתָּא דַּהֲנוּנִיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the list of craving foods to an even smaller item.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even a fragrant date must be shared with the waiter right away.

steps.title: The general rule: smell or sharp taste
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא sums up: any food with a strong smell or a sharp taste must be shared with whoever is there.
steps.simpleTranslation: The rule of the matter: anything that has a smell or has a sharp taste.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gathers all the examples into one simple rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Mushrooms and dates have a strong smell. Turnip in vinegar has a sharp taste. These two qualities are what wake up a craving, so any food with either one may not be held back from the person serving.

keyTerms.meaning: The general rule of the matter
Sharpness, a sharp or sour taste

steps.whatToRemember: You may make a waiter wait for his food, except for any food with a strong smell or a sharp taste. Those stir a craving and must be shared right away.

phrases.english: The rule of the matter:
anything that has a smell
or has a sharp taste.
phrases.notes: The word literally reads "and," but it means either one is enough.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּלָלָא דְמִילְּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sums up all the examples into one principle.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Any food with a strong smell or sharp taste must be shared with the one serving right away.

steps.title: Two brothers: one gave from every dish
steps.stepSummary: אבוה בר איהי and מנימין בר איהי: one gave his waiter from every kind of food, the other from only one kind. אליהו spoke with the first and not with the second.
steps.simpleTranslation: אבוה בר איהי and מנימין בר איהי: one would give from every single kind, and one would give from one kind. אליהו spoke with this one, and אליהו did not speak with that one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story to show how much Heaven cares about feeling for the waiter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both brothers fed their waiter something, but only one shared from every dish. The one who shared from every kind earned visits from אליהו הנביא, and the one who gave from only one kind did not.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבוּהּ בַּר אִיהִי וּמִנְיָמִין בַּר אִיהִי,
phrases.english: Avuh bar Ihi and Minyamin bar Ihi:
one would give from every single kind,
and one would give from one kind.
This Sage, Elijah spoke with him,
and that Sage, Elijah did not speak with him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבוּהּ בַּר אִיהִי וּמִנְיָמִין בַּר אִיהִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the rule to stories showing the reward for being extra careful.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sharing from every dish with the waiter is a mark of piety that earns closeness to אליהו.

steps.title: Two pious men: feeding the waiter first or later
steps.stepSummary: Two חסידים, possibly רב מרי and רב פנחס, the sons of רב חסדא: one fed his waiter first, the other later. אליהו spoke only with the one who fed him first.
steps.simpleTranslation: There were two pious men, and some say they were רב מרי and רב פנחס, the sons of רב חסדא. One gave first, and one gave later. The one who gave first, אליהו spoke with him. The one who gave later, אליהו did not speak with him.
steps.whatsHappening: A second story, this time about timing: when you feed the waiter, not only how much.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The last story was about how many kinds of food. This one is about when. Even though both men fed the waiter, making him wait while others ate meant he suffered, and the one who did that lost the visits of אליהו.
steps.whatToRemember: Both how much you share (from every dish) and when you share (first, not after) show true care for the one who serves you.

phrases.english: There were two pious men,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ: רַב מָרִי וְרַב פִּנְחָס בְּנֵי רַב חִסְדָּא,
phrases.english: and some say they were Rav Mari and Rav Pinchas, the sons of Rav Chisda:

phrases.aramaic: מָר קָדֵים סָפֵי, וּמָר מְאַחַר סָפֵי.
phrases.english: one Sage would give first, and one Sage would give later.
phrases.notes: First means before the meal; later means after everyone else had eaten.

phrases.english: The one who gave first, Elijah spoke with him;

phrases.aramaic: דִּמְאַחַר סָפֵי — לָא מִשְׁתַּעֵי אֵלִיָּהוּ בַּהֲדֵיהּ.
phrases.english: the one who gave later, Elijah did not speak with him.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנְהוּ תַּרְתֵּין חֲסִידֵי, וְאָמְרִי לַהּ: רַב מָרִי וְרַב פִּנְחָס בְּנֵי רַב חִסְדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel story, moving from how much to give to when to give it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Feeding the waiter first, before the meal, is the pious way and earns closeness to אליהו.

steps.title: Three Sages at the king's gate: the story begins
steps.stepSummary: אמימר, מר זוטרא and רב אשי were sitting at the gate of the palace of אזגור מלכא. The king's chief butler passed by, and רב אשי saw something about מר זוטרא.
steps.simpleTranslation: אמימר, מר זוטרא, and רב אשי were sitting at the entrance of the house of אזגור מלכא. The king's chief butler was passing by. רב אשי saw מר זוטרא...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up another story about craving food. It continues on the next amud, so here we only meet the scene.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The butler is carrying the king's food past the Sages, and that fits the topic of food that causes craving. The line stops in the middle, right as רב אשי notices something about מר זוטרא. The point of the story comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: Chief butler, in charge of the king's food
